clinical_text:
CLINIC NOTE
54 y/o man with sudden severe pain, redness and swelling of the right great toe since last night. Uric acid 9.1.
Assessment: Acute gout flare, right great toe.
Plan: Colchicine, NSAID, follow up.

CLINIC NOTE
29 y/o woman with dysuria and urgency for 1 day. No blood in urine, no fever, no flank pain.
UA: positive nitrites.
Assessment: Acute cystitis without hematuria.
Plan: Nitrofurantoin x 5 days.

PEDIATRIC VISIT
8 y/o boy with left ear pain and fever for 2 days. Left tympanic membrane bulging and erythematous. Right ear normal.
Assessment: Acute otitis media, left ear.
Plan: Amoxicillin.

NEUROLOGY
45 y/o woman with episodic unilateral throbbing headaches with nausea, no aura, 3-4 per month, respond to triptans.
Assessment: Migraine without aura, not intractable, without status migrainosus.
Plan: Continue sumatriptan.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
70 y/o man with COPD on home oxygen 2 L admitted with increased dyspnea and sputum. ABG pO2 52 on room air.
Current smoker, 1 pack of cigarettes per day.
Discharge diagnoses:
1. COPD with acute exacerbation
2. Acute on chronic hypoxic respiratory failure
3. Nicotine dependence, cigarettes

PRIMARY CARE
62 y/o woman with essential hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Claudication with walking. ABI 0.7 bilaterally, no ulcers, no gangrene.
Medications: glipizide 5 mg daily, amlodipine.
Assessment:
1. Type 2 diabetes with diabetic peripheral angiopathy without gangrene
2. Essential hypertension

BEHAVIORAL HEALTH
35 y/o man with excessive worry most days for 8 months, restlessness, poor concentration. Also trouble falling asleep.
Assessment:
1. Generalized anxiety disorder
2. Insomnia
Plan: Start sertraline, CBT referral.

HEMATOLOGY
50 y/o woman with fatigue. Hgb 9.2, ferritin 6. Heavy regular menstrual periods for a year.
Assessment: Iron deficiency anemia secondary to chronic blood loss from menorrhagia (excessive menstruation with regular cycle).
Plan: IV iron, gynecology referral.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
40 y/o man rolled his right ankle stepping off a curb. Swelling over the anterior talofibular ligament. X-ray negative for fracture.
Assessment: Sprain of anterior talofibular ligament of right ankle, initial encounter.
Plan: RICE, brace.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
75 y/o woman admitted with fever and left flank pain. Urine and blood cultures grew E. coli. Sodium 127.
Discharge diagnoses:
1. Acute pyelonephritis due to E. coli
2. Hyponatremia

UROLOGY
60 y/o man with nocturia 3 times nightly and weak stream. Prostate enlarged, smooth.
Assessment: Benign prostatic hyperplasia with lower urinary tract symptoms, nocturia.
Plan: Tamsulosin.

CLINIC NOTE
66 y/o postmenopausal woman, DEXA T-score -2.8 at the hip. No fractures.
Medications: alendronate 70 mg weekly for 2 years.
Assessment: Postmenopausal osteoporosis without current pathological fracture.
Plan: Continue alendronate, calcium and vitamin D.

CLINIC NOTE
31 y/o woman with fatigue. 25-OH vitamin D level 14.
Assessment: Vitamin D deficiency.
Plan: Ergocalciferol 50,000 units weekly.

HEPATOLOGY
57 y/o man with chronic hepatitis C, genotype 1a, compensated, no hepatic coma or encephalopathy.
Assessment: Chronic viral hepatitis C.
Plan: Start direct-acting antiviral therapy.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
68 y/o man with hypertension and chronic kidney disease stage 5, not yet on dialysis, admitted with dyspnea and edema. EF 35% with impaired relaxation.
Discharge diagnoses:
1. Acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure
2. Hypertension
3. Chronic kidney disease stage 5

GERIATRIC CLINIC
72 y/o woman with type 2 diabetes, glucose readings 250-300, on insulin glargine long-term. She has fallen twice this year.
Assessment:
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia
2. History of falling
Plan: Adjust insulin, home safety evaluation.

URGENT CARE
24 y/o woman fell while jogging and struck her left knee. Bruising and tenderness, full range of motion, x-ray normal.
Assessment: Contusion of left knee, initial encounter.
Plan: Ice, NSAIDs.

SLEEP REFERRAL
49 y/o man with loud snoring and daytime somnolence. Wife reports pauses in breathing.
Assessment: Snoring and daytime somnolence, rule out obstructive sleep apnea.
Plan: Polysomnography.
